messages.subject: scale_area() and negative values
parts:
Hi again,

scale_area() does not deal with negative values:

qplot(x=1:2, 1:2, size=c(-1,1))
qplot(x=1:2, 1:2, size=c(-1,1)) + scale_area()

It has always been the case I think, but I just used to default to
size=radius rather than size=area. However, currently I would really
need a the enhanced perceptual mapping that scale_area provides.

I understand that this is because scale_area is really just scale size
with a sqrt transformation of the scale. I think I found where in the
code this is specified but I have no clue how to change it (proto is
still impenetrable for me). Would that be something easy enough to
change Hadley? Ideally it should behave as scale_size with respect to
negative values, i.e.
small points for negative values, bigger points for larger, positive
values by default
big points for very negative or very positive values and small points
for 0 when 'to' is specificed

Thanks in advance for your help.

JiHO

value of the minimum negative value), then use the sqrt()

sqrt(x)
}

function(x) {if(any(range(x) < 0 )) x <- x - min(x) ; sqrt(x)})

> somehow they seem to require an inverse transform which cannot be

Well, this is actually what I did (but in a much less elegant way): I
shifted my data above 0. But then, as you notice, the labels in the
legen are wrong, so I hade to recompute them and specify them manually.

Apparently a new transform takes 4 arguments: the name, the
transformation function, the inverse transformation function and the
function to generate labels:

new <- function(., name, f="force", inverse="force",
labels="force", ...) {
.$proto(
objname = name,
.transform = f,
.transform_inverse = inverse,
.transform_labels = labels,
...
)
}

I tried to use attributes to be able to store the minimum and hence
define an inverse transformation:

TransSqrtshift <- Trans$new("sqrtshift",
function(x) {
if(any(range(x) < 0 )) x <- x - min(x);

attr(x,"shiftMin") <- min(x);
sqrt(x)
},
function(x) {
x <- x^2;
return(x + attr(x, "shiftMin"))
},
function(x) {
x <- x^2;
return(x + attr(x, "shiftMin"))
}
)

ScaleSqrtshift <- proto(ScaleContinuous,
desc = "Position scale, shifted and square root transformed",
tr_default = Trans$find("sqrtshift"),
objname = "sqrtshift",
doc=FALSE,
examples=function(.) {}
)

ScaleArea <- proto(
ScaleSize,
desc = "Scale area",
objname = "area",
icon = function(.) ScaleSize$icon(),
details = "",
doc = FALSE,
new = function(., name=NULL, limits=NULL, breaks=NULL, labels=NULL,
to = c(1, 6)) {
.super$new(., name = name, limits = limits, breaks = breaks,
labels = labels, trans="sqrtshift", to = to)
}
)

qplot(x=1:2, y=1:2, size=c(-1,1))
qplot(x=1:2, y=1:2, size=c(-1,1)) + scale_area()
ggplot(data.frame(x=1:2, y=1:2, size=c(-1,1))) +
geom_point(aes(x=x,y=y,size=size)) + scale_area()

I'd probably do it like this:

df <- data.frame(x=1:2, y = 1:2, val=c(-1,5))

qplot(x, y, size = abs(val), colour = factor(sign(val)), data = df) +
scale_area()

That way positive and negative values of the same magnitude have the
same size but different colours.
